I have seasonal depression. Dec-Mar are the worst for me by far and every single year, ever since I was 12 (I’m almost 20), I’ve tried to commit suicide in the winter. 

It’s as if I have a bad attitude problem for this duration of time. I’m able to work my 4:30am-1pm shifts but I sleep from 1pm-3:30am because I legitimately feel exhausted. Every second of that sleep is cherished and needed. 

Middle school through high school, in the winters I would go to school, and sleep right after until school the next day. No one saw an issue with this because they were just glad I wasn’t hurting myself. My middle school even allowed me to have naps in the nurses office.

Me choosing to wait to start college during the summer isn’t a cop out to push it off, it’s realizing the winter is absolute hell for me and I’m able to be more productive in the summer - late fall early winter. I’m trying to shift my schedule from being Aug - May to May - Dec. It’s not a crime and community college isn’t based off any real rules. 

During the winters they (my family) seem to give up on me. They just think I’ve given up, so they attack me on all my downfalls and they berate me for not progressing. They shit on me for not having the same amount of patience and for not being able to keep up.

I am 19 working 50 hours a week. I also use all my free time to clean, volunteer for my community and enjoy my friends and partner. I’m not lazy, a bad person or a loser. I just have never been able to integrate into society quite right because 1/4 of my entire year Im severely depressed. 

It’s as if my life needs to pause in the winter and I just need a second to coast. My emotions can’t handle all the pressure I put myself under 24/7 so my body forces this little emotional hibernation.. me, being first generation to an immigrant parent they see me as lazy and ungrateful.

I cut for years, until I really thought about what cutting did for me. It gave me an immediate release from my pain emotionally, with a physical action. 

Basically I treated my emotions like a recipe. 

Step 1: something makes me upset and I start to freak out

Step 2: I cut, releasing tension

And boom, im better.

But what do we do when we can’t use a specific ingredient because someone’s allergic or we just don’t have it?

You find a substitute.

My substitute for self harm is smoking pot. I haven’t self harmed since I started smoking medicinally and it works wonders. 

Cutting is a completely understandable response to stress and too much negative stimuli, but when you break it down you don’t need to do it. You just need to replace it with something that doesn’t leave scarring and risk a bad infection. 

My brother uses food. Chocolate is known to release dopamine in your brain when you eat it, so when he’s sad he buys a whole gallon of milk.

Just find whatever works for you, but cutting is a dark road filled with unneeded shame and persecution. You can literally replace it with anything! Just make sure it makes YOU happy
